about.title: Fairfield Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Fairfield's most recent final collision data for 2025 records 7 traffic deaths, 645 injury crashes and 912 people injured. Behind each of those seven is a Solano County household trying to figure out what comes next. A wrongful death claim is a civil case, separate from anything the district attorney may pursue, and it exists so a family can recover funeral and burial costs, the income the person would have provided, and compensation for the love, companionship and guidance that is now gone. California limits who may bring the claim: a spouse or registered domestic partner and children come first, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when there is no one in that first group. The clock runs two years from the date of death, and much less when a public agency is involved, which can happen on state-maintained stretches like I-80 or city streets such as Air Base Parkway. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Fairfield families, at no charge, with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Fairfield Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California gives the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a claim, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in other circumstances. The attorney we connect you with can sort out standing before any other step.

items.title: The Deadline Is Real
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is far shorter if a government entity may share fault. Getting connected early protects your options.

items.title: Every Loss Counts
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance are all recoverable under California law. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash happened on I-80 through Fairfield. Does that change anything about the deadline?
items.answer: It might. If a public agency such as Caltrans or the City of Fairfield could be partly responsible for a road condition, a formal government claim generally must be filed within months rather than the usual two years. An attorney can evaluate whether that shorter timeline applies to your situation and act accordingly.

items.question: Do we have to wait for the criminal case against the driver to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, regardless of whether charges are filed or how a criminal case ends. Evidence from the police investigation can still be useful, but the two-year civil deadline keeps running in the meantime.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm, and what does it cost to use?
items.answer: LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Fairfield families with an independent personal injury attorney who handles wrongful death claims. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they are paid only if there is a recovery.
